title: Replaying real Indian incidents
question: If these Indian organisations had asked CyCRS for a plan at a ₹50,000 budget, would its top 3 controls have addressed what actually happened?

data_in.dataset: data/raw/cases.csv: documented Indian incidents from news and government sources

variables.name: sector
variables.transform: Other when outside the model's top 8

variables.name: size_bucket
variables.transform: unknown when the source does not say

variables.name: actual_actions
variables.transform: VERIS action categories stated in the source

prep_steps: Only facts stated in each fetched source were recorded
Each case run through the live engine with no controls in place and a budget of INR 50,000
Verdict compares the action categories the top 3 controls address with the categories the source reports

why: Only 4 Indian incidents are documented well enough to replay, too few for a hit rate, so each case is judged on its own. A verdict per case shows a reader exactly where the advice matches reality and where the source is too thin to judge.

data_properties.name: Cases replayed
data_properties.implication: Small qualitative check, not a statistical test.

data_properties.name: Cases with known attack categories
data_properties.implication: Only these can get a verdict.

data_properties.name: Covered among assessable cases
data_properties.implication: How often the top 3 addressed what happened.

alternatives.model: Coverage hit rate on Indian cases
alternatives.why_not: With 4 cases a rate would swing by 25 points per case; the VCDB hit rate is the statistical check.
Sources that do not state the method are marked not assessable instead of filled in.

assumptions.verdict: unknown size and assets left unknown
assumptions.action_taken: Engine uses its reference levels for unknowns.

yields: For 3 of the 3 cases whose sources say how the attack worked, CyCRS's top 3 controls at INR 50,000 address that kind of attack. 1 case does not state the method, so it is shown without a verdict rather than counted as a success.
limitations: Four public cases from large organisations, not small businesses.
Addressing an attack type does not prove the control would have stopped that incident.
